Mohammed Sadiq Adam Shaikh vs The State Of Maharashtra on
14 August, 2024

Author: Sanjay Kumar
Bench: Sanjay Kumar
 1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. Of 2024
 (arising out of Slp (Crl.) No. 4480 Of 2024)
 Mohammed Sadiq Adam Shaikh ..... Appellant(S)
 Versus
 State Of Maharashtra ..... Respondent(S)
 With
 Criminal Appeal No. Of 2024
 (arising out of Slp (Crl.) No. 7479 of 2024)
 O R D E R
Criminal Appeal @ SLP(CRL.) NO. 4480 OF 2024 Leave granted.

Given the facts and circumstances of the case, where debate persists on whether Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 1 would at all be applicable, we accept the present appeal and direct that if the appellant, Mohammed Sadiq Adam Shaikh, is arrested in connection with First Information Report No. 288 of 2023 dated 02.10.2023 registered with Police Station  Kankavli, District  Sindhudurg, Maharashtra for the offence(s) punishable under Section 328 of the IPC and Sections 26(2)(iv), 27(3)(e), 30(2)(a) and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, he shall be released on bail by the arresting/investigating officer/trial court, on terms 1 For short, IPC.
and conditions to be fixed by the trial court.
In addition, the appellant, Mohammed Sadiq Adam Shaikh, shall comply with the conditions mentioned in Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

CRIMINAL APPEAL @ SLP(CRL.) NO. 7479 OF 2024 Leave granted.

Given the facts and circumstances of the case, where debate persists on whether Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 would be at all applicable, we accept the present appeal and direct that in the event of the appellant, Nayeem Ahmed Khan, being arrested in connection with First Information Report No. 149 of 2022 dated 16.02.2022 registered with Police Station  Yavat,
District  Pune Rural, Maharashtra, for the offence(s) punishable under Sections 188, 272, 273, 328 and 34 of the IPC and Sections 26(2)(i), 26(2)(iv) and 27(2)(e) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, he shall be released on bail by the arresting/investigating officer/trial court, on terms and conditions to be fixed by the trial court.
In addition, the appellant, Nayeem Ahmed Khan, shall comply with the conditions mentioned in Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Recording the aforesaid, the impugned order is set aside and the appeal is allowed.
We clarify that the observations made in this order are for disposal of the present appeal and grant of bail and the same will not be treated as expression of opinion on the merits of the case.

Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

AUGUST 14, 2024.
